stories.headline: Yemen's Houthis Launch Missiles at Saudi Arabia After Strikes on Sanaa Airport
stories.summary:
Yemen's Houthi movement fired ballistic missiles and drones at Abha International Airport in southwestern Saudi Arabia on Monday, following air strikes on Sanaa's international airport that the Houthis blamed on the Saudi-led coalition. The Saudi-led coalition said its air defenses intercepted the incoming fire and reported no casualties. The Houthi military spokesperson warned airlines against flying through Saudi airspace until a "blockade" on Sanaa airport is lifted.

The strikes on Sanaa were claimed by Yemen's internationally recognized government, which said it targeted the airport's runway to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing. The plane was carrying a Houthi delegation returning from Iran after attending the funeral of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The Iranian aircraft ultimately diverted to the Red Sea city of Hudaydah.

Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree declared the incident had ended the "de-escalation phase" of their conflict with Saudi Arabia and vowed the strikes would not go "unanswered or unpunished." Saudi authorities declined to publicly comment on the Sanaa strikes before the Houthi retaliation was announced.

The exchange marks the most significant military escalation between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia since an informal truce took effect four years ago. Yemen's civil war, which began in 2014, has killed more than 150,000 people and left more than 22 million in need of humanitarian aid, according to the United Nations. The fresh hostilities raise concern about a renewed breakdown of the fragile ceasefire.

stories.headline: New York Imposes First-in-the-Nation Statewide Moratorium on Hyperscale Data Centers
stories.summary:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul announced Monday that she is imposing a statewide freeze of up to one year on new environmental permits for "hyperscale" data centers, making New York the first state in the nation to enact such a moratorium. The pause is intended to give state officials time to develop a regulatory framework addressing the impact of large-scale data centers on the environment, the electricity grid, and consumer utility bills.

Hyperscale data centers, which power artificial intelligence applications and cloud computing, have drawn scrutiny nationwide for their enormous energy demands. Hochul's office framed the action as a protective measure for New York residents facing potential rate increases and grid strain as the AI industry rapidly expands its infrastructure footprint.

The move positions New York as a leading edge of state-level pushback against unchecked AI infrastructure growth at a time when federal regulation of the sector remains limited. Critics of such moratoriums have argued they risk slowing economic development and pushing investment to states with fewer environmental constraints.

The one-year pause is expected to affect planned projects from major technology companies that had identified New York as a target for data center expansion. State officials said the moratorium will remain in effect while a new permitting and oversight framework is established.

stories.headline: Update: Cyclospora Outbreak Grows to Nearly 4,000 Cases Across 31 States; Source Still Unidentified
stories.summary:
The parasitic intestinal illness cyclosporiasis has now been reported in 31 states, with nearly 4,000 confirmed cases this summer — a figure substantially higher than previous outbreak seasons. Michigan is bearing the heaviest burden, with more than 2,600 cases including at least 44 hospitalizations. Federal health officials have not yet pinpointed a definitive food or water source driving the outbreak.

Cyclosporiasis is caused by the parasite Cyclospora cayetanensis, typically transmitted through contaminated produce or water. Health experts say the illness is particularly disruptive because watery diarrhea can persist for weeks or months rather than the two to three days typical of most gastrointestinal infections. An incubation period of two to 14 days makes identifying the exposure source especially difficult for both patients and investigators.

The CDC and public health authorities have urged anyone experiencing diarrhea lasting more than two to three days to seek medical testing and treatment. The illness is treatable with antibiotics. Prior outbreaks have been linked to fresh produce items such as cilantro, raspberries, and salad greens, though no single source has been confirmed in the current outbreak.

This is a new development from previously covered reporting: the case count has grown to approximately 4,000 — up from 2,800 — and the geographic spread has widened to 31 states, representing a material escalation in the scale of the outbreak.

stories.headline: Update: Survivor Describes Watching Wife and Friends Die in Spain Wildfire as Death Toll Reaches 13
stories.summary:
Malcolm Timbrell, a 70-year-old British man, recounted Monday how he survived last Thursday's catastrophic wildfire in Bédar, Almeria province, while his wife Annette Kilgore, 69, and at least 12 friends and neighbors are feared dead. Timbrell described returning to their property to retrieve the couple's cats while Annette and their neighbors fled on foot — a decision he said cost them their lives as a firefront moving at more than 20 kilometers per hour overtook them.

Timbrell said he sheltered inside the last of six cars parked near his home as four others burst into flames around him. He survived inside the final vehicle with one of his cats as flames passed. Eight bodies were subsequently found on a path leading from the couple's hillside home. Spanish authorities have confirmed victims include British, French, Belgian, and Spanish nationals.

The Bédar fire is among the deadliest wildfires in Spanish history. Authorities have previously confirmed at least three British fatalities, and a right-hand-drive vehicle found burned at the scene is believed to have carried four additional British victims. The full death toll and identities of all victims have not yet been confirmed.

Spain has experienced extreme wildfire conditions this summer, with several major fires burning across the country. The Almeria blaze has drawn particular attention given the large number of British expatriates living in the region and the speed with which the fire overtook a populated village.

stories.headline: Update: Fed Chair Warsh Testifies on Monetary Policy as Rate-Setting Committee Remains Split
stories.summary:
New Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh appeared before the House Financial Services Committee on Tuesday for the agency's semi-annual monetary policy report, his first major congressional testimony since taking the role. The hearing comes amid elevated inflation driven in part by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, with Brent crude approaching $85 a barrel following the resumption of hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz.

Minutes released last week revealed the Fed's rate-setting committee is divided over the inflation outlook. Many officials projected the benchmark rate — currently at 3.6% — would remain unchanged or fall slightly by year-end, while half of the 18 policymakers who submitted projections supported a rate increase. Warsh declined to submit his own forecast, saying doing so can lock policymakers into positions that become difficult to reverse if conditions shift.

The economic backdrop is challenging: U.S. home prices hit an all-time high median of $440,600 in June even as existing home sales slipped 2.4%, and the IMF last week downgraded global growth to 3% for 2026, citing the energy shock from the Iran war. Warsh has publicly emphasized the Fed's political independence and a focus on taming inflation, themes expected to dominate the congressional hearing.

stories.headline: Update: GOP Challenger Announces Bid for Graham's South Carolina Senate Seat as Succession Process Begins
stories.summary:
Mark Lynch, who lost to Sen. Lindsey Graham in last month's Republican primary, announced Monday he will seek the GOP nomination in the special election to fill Graham's seat. Lynch made the announcement on social platform X, saying he was responding to requests from supporters. The move sets up an early contest for a seat that is central to the Senate's Republican majority.

South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster was expected to announce Monday an interim appointment to fill Graham's seat. President Trump and Sen. Tim Scott had pushed McMaster to appoint Graham's sister, Darline Graham Nordone, as a caretaker. Nordone, who has no prior elected experience, was subsequently appointed. The seat will be contested in a special election whose timing has not yet been set.

Graham's death on Saturday has triggered a succession process with significant implications for Senate dynamics. Graham chaired or held senior roles on key committees and was regarded by Senate Majority Leader John Thune as the "glue" of the Republican caucus. Thune delivered a tearful tribute on the Senate floor Monday as a black veil covered Graham's desk.

stories.headline: Update: Ukraine Fears Loss of Key White House Link After Graham's Death
stories.summary:
Ukrainian officials and lawmakers expressed alarm Monday over the death of Sen. Lindsey Graham, describing him as an irreplaceable intermediary between Kyiv and the Trump White House. Graham had visited Ukraine just two days before his death, standing in Kyiv's St. Michael's Square and promising to advance sweeping new economic sanctions against Russia upon his return to Washington.

Oleksandr Merezhko, a lawmaker with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's party, said Graham was "truly indispensable" and "the closest link between Ukraine, our president and Trump." Zelenskyy, who noted Graham had visited Ukraine 10 times since Russia's full-scale invasion, said he was "deeply saddened" by the senator's sudden death. Ukrainian officials fear the loss will weaken their ability to influence the White House across a range of issues, including the Russia sanctions legislation Graham had championed alongside Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal.

Graham had played a particularly sensitive role given Trump's historically strained relationship with Zelenskyy. With Graham gone, Ukrainian officials said they do not know who in Trump's orbit could fill that role. The fate of the bipartisan Russia sanctions bill, which Graham described as within reach during his final Kyiv visit, is now uncertain.

stories.headline: Update: Bangkok Bar Fire Death Toll Rises to 30 as Investigation Reveals Locked Doors, Flammable Decor
stories.summary:
Thai authorities investigating Sunday's deadly fire at a Bangkok bar confirmed Monday that the death toll has climbed to at least 30, with more than 70 injured and 24 in critical condition. Investigators found that doors near the restrooms were locked, exits were poorly marked, and the stage was decorated with highly flammable plastic flowers while the ceiling was coated in combustible foam — conditions that caused the fire to spread within seconds of igniting.

Preliminary findings point to a short circuit in an air conditioner as the likely ignition source. Survivors reported running toward the back of the venue away from the flames, only to find themselves trapped when the rear door could not be opened. Fire safety experts said many victims likely died from inhaling carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide produced by the burning synthetic materials before flames reached them.

The bar, Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao, was registered as a "restaurant with live music" rather than an entertainment venue, exempting it from requirements to use fire-retardant materials. Bangkok's Metropolitan Administration said it is reviewing regulations governing construction and decoration materials in both categories. The Thai indie band Thotsakan, which was performing when the fire broke out, lost two members in the blaze.
